The user is fascinated by the history of Chinese kites used for military purposes and was surprised by how versatile they were in Song dynasty warfare. #kites #chinese-history #user-interests

Song dynasty military kite uses discussed: signaling to troops, reconnaissance of enemy territory, psychological warfare (dropping messages/objects over enemy camps), distraction with whistles or bells, and as targets for archery practice. #kites #chinese-history

Song dynasty military kites were built with lightweight bamboo frames covered in silk or paper, sometimes shaped as birds or insects for stability, and painted with symbols showing affiliation (e.g., imperial family symbols). #kites #chinese-history

Military kite use spread beyond China: Japan used kites as battle signals (incl. the Boshin War, 1868-1869); Britain and the US used large kites for aerial observation and artillery spotting in WWI/WWII; US troops used light-bearing kites for night illumination in the Korean War. #kites #chinese-history

User asked me to write a harsh-but-fair academic peer review of a paper on community information needs assessments, and to write it in the voice of a journalism and communications researcher critiquing methods and theory. #Peer_Review_Task #NJ_Info_Needs_Paper

Paper under review: a research project, seemingly from the Center for Cooperative Media at Montclair State, assessing information needs of three New Jersey communities served by nascent news outlets funded by the New Jersey Civic Information Consortium (a first-in-the-nation state public funding mechanism begun 2018). #NJ_Info_Needs_Paper

The three outlets/communities studied: Paterson Info Hub (Paterson Alliance + Free Public Library), Trenton Journal (Kenneth Miles, founded 2021), and a Blairstown outlet. NJ Civic Information Consortium grantees. #NJ_Info_Needs_Paper

Methods in the paper: online surveys (Paterson n=67; Trenton n=119) plus in-person focus groups (Paterson: 3 groups, one in Spanish, 3/10/9 participants; Trenton: 2 English groups, 10 and 7 participants). Paterson survey translated into English, Spanish, Arabic, Bengali. #NJ_Info_Needs_Paper

Paper's stated findings: all three communities want "service journalism" (meeting info, service providers, contact lists); heavy reliance on Facebook; Paterson and Trenton want more crime/safety coverage; Paterson and Blairstown could grow audience with non-English content; some demand for solutions-oriented "feel-good" news. #NJ_Info_Needs_Paper

Paper's literature framing: cites Listening Post Collective, Groundsource, Hearken, Outlier Media, Internews; traces lineage to Knight Commission 2009 report and Waldman's 2011 FCC report; cites Alvarez (2021) definition of information needs, Schmidt & Lawrence (2020) on engaged journalism/public journalism, Crittenden & Haywood (2020), Konieczna (2020), McCullough & DeVigal (2022). #NJ_Info_Needs_Paper

Workflow for the review: user sends the paper in five parts; I acknowledged Part 1 (executive summary, intro, Paterson and Trenton sections) and agreed to wait for Parts 2-5 before writing the full review. #Peer_Review_Task
Preliminary critique angles on the NJ information-needs paper: no stated research questions or design justification, and no described analytic or coding method. #NJ_Info_Needs_Paper

Preliminary critique angles: tiny non-probability samples (n=67, n=119), no response rate or sampling frame, one focus group with only 3 participants; "needs" conflated with wants and with publisher strategy. #NJ_Info_Needs_Paper

Critique angle: paper treats residents' heavy Facebook use as an opportunity for publishers, without addressing platform dependency, algorithmic gatekeeping, or misinformation risk it itself acknowledges. #NJ_Info_Needs_Paper

Critique angle: the document's executive-summary style and its framing around what "publishers" should do suggest a consulting report rather than peer-reviewed scholarship; contributions to theory are unstated. #NJ_Info_Needs_Paper

On 2023/05/28 (Sunday) evening the user was researching tax/payee forms: IRS W-9, IRS W-7, and a state form they were filling out. #forms #taxpaperwork

IRS Form W-9 is used by a payor to collect a payee's taxpayer identification number (TIN) so payments can be reported to the IRS (e.g., on Form 1099). It asks for name, business name, address, TIN, and a certification of taxpayer status. #forms #W9

IRS Form W-7 is used by nonresident aliens/foreign nationals who are not eligible for a Social Security number to apply for an ITIN for tax filing. It requires identity/foreign-status documents such as a passport, plus a valid federal return unless an exception applies. An ITIN is not work authorization. #forms #W7 #ITIN

California STD 204 is officially titled "Payee Data Record"; California state agencies use it to collect a payee's name, address, and TIN for state/federal tax reporting when setting up or updating a payee. #forms #STD204 #California

The user said the form they were dealing with is a "bidder declaration" rather than the STD 204 Payee Data Record. The assistant guessed this was California's GSPD-05-105 Bidder Declaration, but that identification was never confirmed by the user. #forms #California #BidderDeclaration

Argentina borders five countries — Chile, Bolivia, Paraguay, Brazil, Uruguay — and their musical traditions shaped Argentine music. Chile's Nueva Canción (1960s, socially aware folk) inspired Argentina's Canción Protesta; Brazilian bossa nova and samba rhythms were fused into tango (Bossa Nova Tango). #argentina-music #music

Beyond tango, Argentine music drew on: Andean music from Bolivia/Peru (charango, quena, zampona), Guarani music from Paraguay (Guarani harp, popular in Argentina's northern provinces), Afro-Argentine genres (murga, candombe, comparsa), and Brazilian-influenced electronic fusions (electro-brega, technobrega). #argentina-music #music

Tango is Argentina's most globally influential music/dance export: popular in France, Japan, Russia; Tango Nuevo modernized it. Argentina also exported rock (Soda Stereo, hugely influential across Latin America) and folk (Soledad Pastorutti). #argentina-music #tango

Argentine electronic artists I recommended: Gustavo Cerati (electronic rock pioneer, ex-Soda Stereo), Zizek Club (Buenos Aires collective, cumbia-electronica), Chancha Via Circuito (electronic + cumbia/chamamé/huayno, international following), Louta (electro-pop), Catnapp (Berlin-based electro/hip-hop). #argentina-music #music

Argentine tango dance spread worldwide from working-class Buenos Aires roots (late 1800s), took off in Europe/US in the early 1900s, and spawned ballroom tango; today there are tango festivals and studios globally plus contemporary/fusion styles. #argentina-music #tango
